title: Crisp Pita Fattoush with Sumac
summary: A Lebanese bread salad built around pita baked until properly crisp, tossed at the last minute with crunchy raw vegetables, herbs and a garlicky lemon dressing, then finished with sumac. Timing the toss is everything here.
equipment: baking tray with a wire rack (or just the tray)

ingredients.item: pita breads (about 120 g), split into 2 thin rounds each
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
romaine heart (about 250 g), cut into 2 cm strips
ripe tomatoes, cut into 2 cm pieces
red onion (about ½ small), thinly sliced

steps.title: Bake the pita
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Lay the thin pita rounds rough side up on the rack set over the tray, brush with the 2 tbsp olive oil, and bake for 10-14 minutes until crisp right through and pale golden. Baking drives off the remaining moisture in the bread, which is what lets it stay crunchy once it meets the dressing later. Let the pita cool, then break it into 2 cm pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: While the pita bakes, whisk the lemon juice, grated garlic and salt together in the small bowl and leave for 10 minutes. The acid in the lemon juice mellows the raw sharpness of the garlic, taking the edge off before it goes anywhere near the salad. Whisk in the dried mint, 4 tbsp olive oil and the pepper.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Put the romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, red onion, spring onions, parsley and mint into the very large bowl. Keeping everything in one big bowl now means it's ready to toss quickly once the pita and dressing join it.

steps.title: Toss just before serving
steps.text: Just before you're ready to eat, add the baked pita pieces and the dressing to the vegetables and toss lightly with your hands until everything is glossy. Tossing at the very last moment matters, as the bread starts wicking up the dressing and softening the moment it's dressed.

steps.title: Finish with sumac
steps.text: Taste the salad for salt, pile it into a serving bowl, and sprinkle over the sumac for its fruity, tangy finish. Serve immediately, while the pita still has its crunch.

tips: Adding the pita too early is the classic fattoush mistake — toss it through with the dressing only right before serving or it turns soggy.
Let the garlic sit in the lemon juice for the full 10 minutes to take the raw bite off before it goes into the dressing.
Bake the pita until properly crisp right through; underbaked pieces soften almost instantly once dressed.
Slice the red onion thinly so it doesn't overpower the other vegetables.
If you're prepping ahead, keep the baked pita, vegetables and dressing separate until the last minute.
storage: This salad doesn't keep well once tossed, as the pita softens quickly; eat it the same day it's dressed. If you do have leftovers, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 1 day, expecting the pita to have lost its crunch; it isn't suitable for freezing.
